subject: Throughput decay impacting production traffic - investigation and next steps
messages:
From: Andrew Stokes <andrew.stokes@acme-corp.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Cc: ops+oncall@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Production latency/backpressure — throughput falling since 14:00 UTC

Hi team,

We're seeing a steady drop in successful throughput to Redwood endpoints starting ~14:00 UTC today. P95/P99 latency jumps, and some customer transactions are timing out (5s+). Our oncall noticed queue depth climbing and many requests in inflight state. This is affecting our checkout flow for a subset of customers (~3% of traffic).

Attached is a Grafana screenshot and a dump from our observability agent showing the request backlog. Can you confirm whether this is on your side ( autoscaler / concurrency caps / backpressure ) or a change on our side? We kicked off a rollback on a small feature just in case.

We need an initial response and ETA for mitigation. Due to SLA exposure, our procurement folks are on this thread.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Stokes
CTO, Acme Corporation
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:38:12 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Production latency/backpressure — throughput falling since 14:00 UTC

Marissa / Rishi — can you take point on this? Initial ask: confirm whether this is due to concurrency caps or an autoscaler reaction that left capacity wobbly. Marissa, please pull recent rollout logs for Acme (ACME-2024-EXP1) and any policy changes for routing/fallback since last Thursday. Rishi, please start with the model pool metrics and the serving nodes' queue lengths; prioritize P95/P99 traces between 13:45-15:30 UTC.

I'll brief Laura after first set of findings; we may need to escalate to Execs if it's a platform regression. Please keep customer updated with a short note within 20 minutes.

-David
David Kim
Account Exec — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:55:46 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency/backpressure — throughput falling since 14:00 UTC

Quick summary of what I see so far (first-pass diagnostics):

- At ~13:58 UTC we saw a short-lived spike in concurrent active inflight requests to Acme's assigned model pool. The spike correlates with a small traffic burst from Acme's EU region (likely a regional fan-in).
- Autoscaler reacted but then transiently dropped available worker count by ~30% due to a mis-evaluation of pod readiness (we had a noisy readiness probe on a recent infra image). That created a window where concurrency caps were binding.
- During that window, the serving runtime applied backpressure and queued requests; the queuing policy moves some requests to a degraded fallback queue which increases P99. If the queue holds beyond token-time budget, front-end returns 504s/timeouts.

Actions taken:
- Increased soft concurrency cap for Acme's pool from 120 -> 200 while we stabilize (temporary override).
- Redeployed a warm worker with corrected readiness probe; now 95% of nodes report healthy.
- Collected inflight queue dump and attached (inflight_queue_dump_20270503.json).

Prelim impact estimate: ~2–4% of overall requests experienced >3s additional queuing; error rate spiked to 1.8% for 15 minutes. No data loss.

Next: run targeted replay of delayed requests against local traces to validate correctness. If the fix holds I suggest keeping the elevated cap for 4 hours and then rolling back once stable.

- Rishi
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Stokes <andrew.stokes@acme-corp.com>, ops+oncall@acme-corp.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 18:02:05 +0000
Subject: Re: Production latency/backpressure — throughput falling since 14:00 UTC

Andrew — quick update from our side: our engineering team identified a transient autoscaler mis-evaluation tied to a recent infra image readiness probe. That caused a temporary reduction in worker count and made the configured concurrency cap bind during a traffic spike. Rishi pushed a hotfix (probe correction) and we've temporarily raised Acme's soft concurrency cap while we watch. Attached are the diagnostic snapshot and Grafana link.

Impact: short window (≈15m) where P99 spiked and a small percentage of requests timed out. We're not seeing persistent degradation after the fix; we've been monitoring for ~2.5 hours and metrics are back to baseline.

Next steps:
- We'll keep Acme on the elevated soft cap for 4 hours and then test rollback in a canary first.
- We'll run a short regression test against your traffic trace and share results by 22:00 UTC.
- Laura / Jonas: we'd like approval to issue a one-time service credit under the SLA for the affected window (ACME-2024-EXP1). Please advise.

Apologies for the incident — we'll follow up with a short postmortem.

-David
From: Andrew Stokes <andrew.stokes@acme-corp.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: ops+oncall@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 18:27:33 +0000
Subject: Re: Production latency/backpressure — throughput falling since 14:00 UTC

Thanks for the quick triage. Appreciate the transparency and the temporary cap increase. Two asks:
1) Confirm the rollback plan and canary schedule before you lower the cap so we can align our traffic shaping.
2) Confirm the size of the proposed one-time service credit (we'll route to procurement once you propose).

If you can get the regression replay and postmortem by tomorrow morning that would help our risk review.

- Andrew
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 20:10:00 +0000
Subject: Exec summary and recommended customer remediation (Acme)

Laura / Jonas — short exec summary and recommendation for approval:

Summary:
- Root cause: autoscaler mis-eval caused by noisy readiness probe in infra image -> temporary worker deficit -> concurrency cap binding during traffic spike -> queued requests -> P99/timeouts.
- Scope: Acme only; ~15 minute window; error rate peaked at 1.8%; estimated affected transactions ~3% of their checkout flow during the window.
- Fix: probe correction + temporary cap increase. Metrics returned to baseline within ~2.5 hours.

Recommendation:
- Approve a one-time credit equivalent to 5% of May's invoice for impacted window (subject to Procurement review).
- Authorize keeping elevated soft cap for 4 hours and then performing a canary rollback; if stable, revert.
- Direct Rishi to produce a 24h postmortem with timeline, monitoring gaps, and a permanent mitigation (autoscaler readiness change + canary for infra image).

If you approve the credit, I'll propose the amount to Acme's procurement and send a short postmortem draft to Andrew tomorrow morning.

-David
